```{r, include = FALSE}
pkgs <- c("parsnip", "recipes", "workflows", "workflowsets", "rsample",
          "tune", "yardstick", "dials", "hardhat")
have <- all(vapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = have,
                      message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
options(digits = 4)
```

[tidymodels](https://www.tidymodels.org/) is a family of packages for
building, resampling, tuning and comparing models with one interface.
flexCountReg plugs into it through **parsnip**: `count_reg()` is a model
specification, and every estimator of the package is one of its *engines*.
A negative binomial regression, a latent-class model and a random-effects
model can then share the same preprocessing, the same resamples and the
same metrics.

This article covers fitting and predicting, recipes and workflows, offsets
and other special columns, comparing and tuning models, weights, panel
models, several outcomes, and getting back to the functions of flexCountReg.

```{r setup}
library(parsnip)
library(recipes)
library(workflows)
library(workflowsets)
library(rsample)
library(tune)
library(yardstick)
library(flexCountReg)

data("washington_roads")
roads <- tibble::as_tibble(washington_roads)
roads$ID <- as.character(roads$ID)
```

`library(tidymodels)` loads all of these except flexCountReg at once. The data have
three years of crashes on each road segment, identified by `ID`.

## A first model

Choose the distribution with `family`, the estimator with `set_engine()`, and
fit. Arguments of the estimator go into `set_engine()`.

```{r first}
nb_spec <- count_reg(family = "NB2") |>
  set_engine("flexCountReg", method = "BFGS")

nb_fit <- fit(nb_spec, Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength + speed50,
              data = roads)
tidy(nb_fit)
glance(nb_fit)
```

Predictions are tibbles with one row per row of `new_data`:

```{r first-predict}
new_roads <- roads[1:4, ]
predict(nb_fit, new_roads)
predict(nb_fit, new_roads, type = "conf_int")
predict(nb_fit, new_roads, type = "pred_int", level = 0.9)
augment(nb_fit, new_roads)[, c(".pred", ".resid", "Total_crashes")]
```

`conf_int` is an interval for the expected count, `pred_int` for a future
count. All engines have them except `countreg_fe`. Everything else that
`predict()` offers is available with `type = "raw"` and `opts`, such as the
probabilities of 0 to 3 crashes. `counts` chooses the counts, so a range such
as `5:8` works too; `overflow = TRUE` (and `underflow = TRUE`) add the
probabilities beyond the range:

```{r first-raw}
predict(nb_fit, new_roads, type = "raw",
        opts = list(type = "prob", counts = 0:3, overflow = TRUE))
```

## The engines

```{r engines}
show_engines("count_reg")
```

| Engine | Estimator | Typical engine arguments |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `flexCountReg` | `countreg()` | `dis_param_formula_1`, `zero_formula`, `underreport_formula`, `offset` |
| `countreg_rp` | `countreg_rp()` | `rpar_formula`, `rpardists`, `ndraws`, `group_var` |
| `countreg_mix` | `countreg_mix()` | `components`, `mixing_formula` |
| `countreg_lc` | `countreg_lc()` | `classes`, `membership_formula`, `group_var` |
| `countreg_fe` | `countreg_fe()` | `fixef` |
| `countreg_hier` | `countreg_hier()` | `re_dist`, `fit_engine` |
| `countreg_alloc` | `countreg_alloc()` | `alloc_formula`, `link` |
| `countreg_mv` | `countreg_mv()` | `copula`, `rpar_formula` |
| `renb`, `repois`, `poislind_re` | the function of that name | `group_var` |
| `negmultinom` | `negmultinom()` | `group_var` |

Two engine arguments belong to the tidymodels interface:

* `predict_args` is a list of arguments for the model's `predict()` method,
  used for numeric predictions, for example
  `predict_args = list(method = "Exact")` for random parameters.
* `fit_engine` is the estimators' own `engine` argument (the numerical
  method), because `set_engine()` already has an argument of that name.

## Recipes and workflows

A **workflow** bundles preprocessing with the model. Here a recipe centers
and scales the numeric predictors and makes indicators of a factor; the
statistics are estimated on the training data only.

```{r workflow}
roads$year <- factor(roads$Year)
set.seed(2026)
split <- group_initial_split(roads, group = ID, prop = 0.75)
train <- training(split)
test <- testing(split)

rec <- recipe(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength + speed50 + year,
              data = train) |>
  step_normalize(lnaadt, lnlength) |>
  step_dummy(year)

nb_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec) |>
  add_model(nb_spec)
nb_wf_fit <- fit(nb_wf, train)
tidy(nb_wf_fit)

augment(nb_wf_fit, test) |>
  rmse(truth = Total_crashes, estimate = .pred)
```

The split keeps all years of a segment on one side (`group_initial_split()`),
so the test segments are new to the model. A random split of rows would put
years of one segment on both sides.

flexCountReg's own `rmse()` and `mae()` take two vectors; given a data
frame they call the yardstick metric, so tidymodels code works whichever
package is loaded last. (With yardstick loaded last, use
`flexCountReg::rmse()` or `yardstick::rmse_vec()` for two vectors.)

## Offsets and other columns that are not predictors

With `add_formula()` or a recipe, all predictors enter the mean model. Count
models often need columns with another purpose: an exposure, a grouping
variable, or a covariate of the dispersion only. A workflow passes the model
only its predictors and outcomes, so these columns must be among the
*predictors* (a recipe's other roles do not reach the model). There are two
ways to say what they are.

**Give the model formula** in `add_model()`. The preprocessor says which
columns are available and the formula says how they are used. All the formula
features of the package work here: `offset()`, smooths `s(x)`, `tv()` terms
and random effects.

```{r offset-formula}
wf_offset <- workflow() |>
  add_variables(outcomes = Total_crashes,
                predictors = c(lnaadt, lnlength, speed50)) |>
  add_model(count_reg() |>
              set_engine("flexCountReg", method = "BFGS",
                         dis_param_formula_1 = ~ lnlength),
            formula = Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + speed50 + offset(lnlength))
tidy(fit(wf_offset, train))[, 1:4]
```

A recipe works too, in place of `add_variables()`:

```{r offset-recipe, eval = FALSE}
workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec) |>
  add_model(nb_spec, formula = Total_crashes ~ s(lnaadt) + speed50)
```

**Name the columns in engine arguments**. Columns named in `offset`,
`group_var`, `panel_id`, `cluster`, `fixef`, `cre_group` or `time` are left
out of the mean model when no model formula is given. So are the
variables of `rpar_formula` with the `countreg_rp` engine, which are random
instead of fixed.

```{r offset-arg}
wf_offset2 <- workflow() |>
  add_formula(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength) |>
  add_model(count_reg() |> set_engine("flexCountReg", method = "BFGS",
                                      offset = "lnlength"))
tidy(fit(wf_offset2, train))[, 1:4]
```

Variables used only in `dis_param_formula_1`, `zero_formula` and similar
formulas are *not* left out, because they often belong in both places; use
a model formula for those. Do not normalize an offset or make indicators of
a grouping column in a recipe.

## Comparing models on resamples

Cross-validate with whole segments, and compare several engines in a
workflow set. The panel engines receive the segment as `group_var`.

```{r workflowset}
set.seed(2026)
folds <- group_vfold_cv(train, group = ID, v = 3)

specs <- list(
  poisson = count_reg(family = "POISSON") |>
    set_engine("flexCountReg", method = "BFGS"),
  nb2 = nb_spec,
  two_class = count_reg(family = "POISSON") |>
    set_engine("countreg_lc", classes = 2, n_starts = 3, seed = 1,
               group_var = "ID"),
  re_poisson = count_reg() |>
    set_engine("repois", group_var = "ID", method = "BFGS"))

base <- workflow_set(
  preproc = list(base = Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength + speed50 + ID),
  models = specs[c("two_class", "re_poisson")])
plain <- workflow_set(
  preproc = list(base = Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength + speed50),
  models = specs[c("poisson", "nb2")])

res <- dplyr::bind_rows(base, plain) |>
  workflow_map("fit_resamples", resamples = folds,
               metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))
rank_results(res, rank_metric = "rmse")[, c("wflow_id", ".metric", "mean",
                                            "std_err")]
```

RMSE and MAE only look at the expected count, and models with the same mean
structure are hard to tell apart by them. To compare the *distributions*,
score the predicted probabilities. `fit_resamples_counts()` resamples a
workflow or specification like `fit_resamples()` and can add the mean
log probability of the held-out counts (larger is better). See
`vignette("predictive-validation", package = "flexCountReg")` for scores and
calibration.

```{r logscore}
f <- Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength + speed50
scores <- lapply(specs, fit_resamples_counts, resamples = folds,
                 formula = f, log_score = TRUE)
do.call(rbind, Map(function(s, nm) {
  cbind(model = nm, s[s$.metric == "log_score", c("mean", "std_err")])
}, scores, names(scores)))
```

## Tuning

The distribution is a tuning parameter:

```{r tune-family}
tune_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_formula(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength + speed50) |>
  add_model(count_reg(family = tune()) |>
              set_engine("flexCountReg", method = "BFGS"))

tuned <- tune_grid(tune_wf, resamples = folds,
                   grid = data.frame(family = c("POISSON", "NB1", "NB2",
                                                "PL")),
                   metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))
show_best(tuned, metric = "rmse")

final_wf <- finalize_workflow(tune_wf, select_best(tuned, metric = "rmse"))
last_fit(final_wf, split, metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)) |>
  collect_metrics()
```

Some engine arguments have tuning parameters too (see `?count_family`):
`components` and `classes`, `zero_type`, `correlated` and `re_dist`. Any
other argument can be tuned with an explicit grid.

```{r tune-classes}
lc_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_formula(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength) |>
  add_model(count_reg(family = "POISSON") |>
              set_engine("countreg_mix", components = tune(), n_starts = 2,
                         seed = 1))
hardhat::extract_parameter_set_dials(lc_wf)
tune_grid(lc_wf, folds, grid = data.frame(components = 2:3),
          metrics = metric_set(rmse)) |>
  collect_metrics()
```

Tuning selects for out-of-sample accuracy; the standard errors of the selected
model do not account for the selection. Some families have no dispersion
parameter, so a grid that includes `"POISSON"` fails for those rows when
`dis_param_formula_1` is set.

Use a parallel backend for slow models
(`future::plan("multisession")` before `tune_grid()`); the workers load
flexCountReg themselves.

## Case weights

Case weights become the estimator's `weights`, by default frequency
weights. parsnip passes the engine only the values of the weights, so for
importance or sampling weights say so with `weight_type = "sampling"`
(`flexCountReg` and `countreg_rp` engines), which gives robust standard
errors.

```{r weights}
train_w <- train
train_w$w <- hardhat::frequency_weights(rep(1:2, length.out = nrow(train)))
wf_w <- workflow() |>
  add_formula(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength) |>
  add_case_weights(w) |>
  add_model(nb_spec)
tidy(fit(wf_w, train_w))[, 1:4]
```

## Panel and hierarchical models

Random effects of `countreg_hier()` are written in the model formula:

```{r hier}
hier_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_variables(outcomes = Total_crashes,
                predictors = c(lnaadt, lnlength, ID)) |>
  add_model(count_reg(family = "NB2") |>
              set_engine("countreg_hier",
                         predict_args = list(marginal = TRUE)),
            formula = Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength + (1 | ID))
hier_fit <- fit(hier_wf, train)
predict(hier_fit, test[1:3, ])
```

The test segments are new groups. With `marginal = TRUE` their predictions
average over the distribution of the random effect; without it they are for a
segment whose effect is zero. The choice matters for `rmse()`, so set it in
`predict_args`. Likewise, `countreg_fe()` has no effect for a new group and
predicts `NA` unless `predict_args = list(newgroup = "mean_fe")`.

A random-parameters model:

```{r rp}
rp_spec <- count_reg(family = "NB2") |>
  set_engine("countreg_rp", rpar_formula = ~ -1 + lnlength,
             ndraws = 100, predict_args = list(method = "Exact"))
rp_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_formula(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + speed50 + lnlength) |>
  add_model(rp_spec)
rp_fit <- fit(rp_wf, train)
tidy(rp_fit)[, 1:4]
predict(rp_fit, test[1:3, ])
```

## Several outcomes

`countreg_mv()` and `countreg_alloc()` model several counts. Declare all of
them as outcomes and give the model formula. There is one prediction column
per outcome.

```{r mv}
set.seed(1)
sev <- train
sev$injury <- rbinom(nrow(sev), sev$Total_crashes, 0.35)
sev$pdo <- sev$Total_crashes - sev$injury

mv_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_variables(outcomes = c(injury, pdo),
                predictors = c(lnaadt, lnlength)) |>
  add_model(count_reg(family = "NB2") |>
              set_engine("countreg_mv", copula = "frank"),
            formula = cbind(injury, pdo) ~ lnaadt + lnlength)
mv_fit <- fit(mv_wf, sev)
predict(mv_fit, sev[1:3, ])
```

(The severities here are simulated.) Interval predictions have a pair of
columns per outcome:

```{r mv-int}
predict(mv_fit, sev[1:3, ], type = "pred_int", level = 0.9)
```

The resampling functions of tune compute metrics for a single outcome.
`fit_resamples_counts()` evaluates all of them:

```{r mv-validate}
mv_folds <- group_vfold_cv(sev, group = ID, v = 3)
fit_resamples_counts(mv_wf, mv_folds, log_score = TRUE)
```

## Back to flexCountReg

`extract_fit_engine()` returns the flexCountReg model, for everything that
tidymodels has no interface for: marginal effects, CURE plots, rootograms,
robust covariances, model tests.

```{r engine, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
m <- extract_fit_engine(fit(wf_offset, train))
margEffTable(m)
cureplot(m, indvar = "lnaadt")
sqrt(diag(vcov(m, type = "robust")))[1:3]
```

Keep in mind:

* Without a model formula the outcome is called `..y` in the extracted model;
  with one it keeps its name.
* The extracted model sees the *preprocessed* columns. Marginal effects after
  `step_normalize()` are per standard deviation.
* A workflow removes the outcome from `new_data`. Predictions that use
  it, such as Empirical Bayes predictions
  (`predict(m, newdata, method = "Individual")`) or posterior class
  probabilities, need the extracted model.
* `keep_data = FALSE` (an engine argument of most estimators) makes saved
  models smaller, at the cost of the functions that need the training data.
* Load flexCountReg before using a saved workflow: that registers the engines.
